skill.name: diffdock
skill.description: Guide DiffDock protein-ligand docking workflows, from setup and batch input preparation to confidence score interpretation and result export.
skill.summary: Run and interpret DiffDock molecular docking workflows for protein-ligand pose prediction.
skill.author: K-Dense-AI

security_audit.summary: The static findings are mainly Markdown command examples, public reference URLs, and user-directed helper script input or output. I found no covert network calls, credential access, prompt injection, or unauthorized command execution, but the skill contains one low-risk external platform promotion that should be reviewed.

remediation.issue: External hosted platform promotion in skill instructions
remediation.suggestion: Remove proactive promotion or make it opt-in with a clear privacy note before users move research data to the hosted service.

remediation.issue: Optional installation commands are shown in documentation
remediation.suggestion: Label Docker, git, and package setup commands as examples that require explicit user approval before execution.

remediation.issue: Helper scripts can write user-selected output files
remediation.suggestion: Warn before overwriting existing files and keep exported reports inside a user-approved workspace path by default.

content.value_statement: Protein-ligand docking requires careful setup, parameter choices, and result interpretation. This skill guides DiffDock workflows for poses, confidence scores, and screening.
actual_capabilities: Explains single protein-ligand docking with PDB, protein sequence, SMILES, SDF, and MOL2 inputs.
Guides batch CSV preparation and validation for multiple protein-ligand complexes.
Describes DiffDock confidence score ranges and how to rank predicted poses.
Provides parameter guidance for samples, inference steps, temperature settings, and batch size.
Documents integration patterns with GNINA, OpenMM, and other downstream scoring tools.
Includes helper scripts for setup checks, batch input creation, and result summary export.
limitations: It does not predict binding affinity, Kd, Ki, or delta G directly.
It depends on a local DiffDock installation, model checkpoints, and scientific Python packages.
GPU hardware is strongly recommended for practical runtime.
Predictions need expert review, visualization, and experimental validation before decisions.

use_cases.title: Dock One Candidate Ligand
use_cases.description: Prepare a protein target and ligand input, run DiffDock, and inspect the top predicted binding poses.

use_cases.title: Screen A Compound Set
use_cases.description: Build and validate a batch input table, run multiple docking jobs, and rank outputs by confidence score.

use_cases.title: Tune Docking Parameters
use_cases.description: Adjust sampling, inference steps, and temperature settings for flexible ligands or difficult protein systems.

prompt_templates.title: Begin Single Docking
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me dock one ligand to one protein with DiffDock. I have a PDB file and a SMILES string.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare Batch Inputs
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a DiffDock batch plan for these protein-ligand pairs and tell me how to validate the CSV before docking.

prompt_templates.title: Interpret Docking Results
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my DiffDock confidence scores and pose files. Explain which predictions are most reliable and what needs validation.

prompt_templates.title: Optimize A Screening Workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Design an efficient DiffDock virtual screening workflow with precomputed embeddings, sampling choices, and downstream rescoring.

output_examples.input: Dock aspirin against a prepared protein target and explain the expected outputs.
output_examples.output: The response lists required inputs, recommends a single-complex DiffDock run, and explains ranked pose files plus confidence scores.

output_examples.input: I have 200 ligands for one target protein. Plan a screening workflow.
output: Create a batch input table with one row per ligand.
Validate protein paths, ligand descriptions, and required columns.
Precompute protein embeddings for repeated target use.
Rank poses by confidence, then rescore and inspect top candidates.

output_examples.input: My top DiffDock scores are all low. What should I try next?
output_examples.output: The response explains likely causes, suggests more samples and ensemble docking, and warns that confidence is not binding affinity.

best_practices: Validate protein structures, ligand formats, and batch CSV files before starting long docking jobs.
Generate multiple samples and inspect top poses visually before downstream scoring.
Use confidence scores for triage, then confirm with rescoring, controls, and experiments.
anti_patterns: Treating DiffDock confidence as binding affinity or final activity evidence.
Running large virtual screens before testing one known protein-ligand case.
Ignoring missing residues, unrealistic protonation states, or poor ligand preparation.

faq.question: Does this skill predict binding affinity?
faq.answer: No. It predicts binding poses and model confidence. Use separate scoring or experimental assays for affinity.

faq.question: Can I use a protein sequence instead of a PDB file?
faq.answer: Yes. DiffDock can use ESMFold to create a structure from sequence, but this adds runtime and uncertainty.

faq.question: What inputs are supported for ligands?
faq.answer: The skill documents SMILES strings and structure files such as SDF or MOL2 when supported by RDKit.

faq.question: Is a GPU required?
faq.answer: A GPU is not strictly required, but CPU runs can be too slow for practical docking or screening.

faq.question: How should I use confidence scores?
faq.answer: Use them to rank and triage poses. Review structures and use complementary scoring before making decisions.

faq.question: Can this handle virtual screening?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill includes batch CSV guidance and recommends precomputed embeddings for repeated target screening.
